safety.what: Every boolean `[features]` key resolves through one table-driven path in which the requirements tier outranks everything else. `Feature::resolve` chains the tiers and `resolve_bool_flag` returns them in a fixed order - requirement, cli, env, config, managed, remote/feature-flag, then the compiled default - so a requirements pin wins in both directions and a user-writable layer can never re-enable what an admin disabled (xai-grok-config-types/src/registry.rs:296-304; src/flags.rs:107-135). The registry is a table of feature specs, each naming its key, config path, environment variable, default and optional remote projection, so adding a feature means adding a row rather than inventing a resolution path (registry.rs:53-64, :86-240). Two knobs deliberately break out of the ladder and use bespoke resolvers because they are security-relevant: the egress gate walks mdm > system-requirements > user-requirements > managed > system-managed > user and has NO environment variable and NO remote tier at all, and the zero-data-retention access flag puts requirements first over env, config, managed and remote (xai-grok-shell/src/util/config/resolve/features.rs:7-24, :97-148).
invariants: The egress gate must exclude the config-overlay environment variable and campaign overlays from its walk, because it is an egress control and soft user-tier input must not be able to re-enable it.
That gate reads the layers first-match rather than the effective merged config, precisely because the merge puts user above managed - reading the merge would invert the intended precedence.
On a config-load error the requirements and managed tiers must still be consulted, so a corrupt user file cannot drop a policy pin.
A requirement pin must win in both directions: it can neither be overridden upward by a user nor downward by an absent value.
safety.failurePolicy: mixed - the egress gate fails OPEN on genuinely absent policy (it defaults to enabled), and the user config tier is fail-open by design, while a requirement pin always wins. The feature registry itself defaults per row with six rows deliberately defaulting OFF, including LSP tools, web fetch and write-file.

safety.name: config-overlay-confinement-allowlist
safety.what: The process-environment config overlay is confined by a fail-closed allowlist rather than trusted wholesale. Only a small fixed set of paths survives the overlay - model selection, features, one toolset field, the two web-search domain lists and four shell-environment-policy filter fields - and everything else is discarded before the overlay is applied (xai-grok-config/src/config_override.rs:106-132). A separate strip list removes security-relevant sections entirely from patch and campaign inputs: version overrides, campaigns, the auth provider and model providers for patches, plus the whole auth and vendor-config sections for campaigns (config_override.rs:77-98). Security gates that must not see overlay influence read a deliberately overlay-free view of the config instead (config_layers.rs:150-153).
invariants: The allowlist is the control, so a new overlay-settable path is a deliberate policy decision rather than an incidental one.
Auth, provider and version-override sections must stay stripped from campaign inputs, or a campaign could redirect authentication.
Security-sensitive readers must use the overlay-free view, not the effective config, so the overlay cannot influence a policy decision even for an allowlisted path.
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed - anything not explicitly allowlisted is dropped from the overlay rather than passed through.

constants.name: OVERLAY_ALLOW_PATHS
constants.value: models, features, toolset.bash.login_shell_capture, two web-search domain lists, four shell_environment_policy filter fields

safety.name: build-provenance-folder-trust-gate
safety.what: Whether a repository's project-scoped hooks, MCP servers, language servers and plugins are allowed to load at all is decided by a folder-trust store, and that gate is itself disabled by build provenance rather than by configuration. `folder_trust_inert()` is defined as `is_local_build()`, which tests whether the version stamp was absent at compile time; the feature check short-circuits to false for a local build BEFORE reading any environment, config or managed value, with the stated reason that even an explicit opt-in is ignored so a self-built binary never prompts (xai-grok-workspace/src/folder_trust.rs:111-145). The release-stamped precedence is environment, then user config, then managed, then remote, defaulting to enabled (folder_trust.rs:151-157). Trust state lives in the user's grok home, never the repository, so a cloned repo cannot self-trust.
invariants: The trust store must live outside the repository: a cloned project cannot be allowed to add itself.
A runtime escape hatch treats a stamped version as a release build for test purposes; without it every test and CI run looks like a local build and the gate appears inert.
The build-provenance short-circuit must stay BEFORE any config read, or a local build could be made to prompt by setting an environment variable.
The hook disable check and its display counterpart must implement the same predicate, or the hooks interface misreports what will run.
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed for an untrusted folder in a release build (project hooks, MCP, LSP and plugins do not load) and deliberately inert in a local build (project scope always allowed, no store I/O at all).

safety.name: managed-mcp-and-marketplace-denylists
safety.what: Managed settings fold every managed-config and requirements layer plus a vendor managed-settings file into MCP-server and plugin-marketplace allow and deny policy, strictest-wins, and the layers are TIERED and sorted before application so a user-writable layer or the advisory vendor file can never claim a marketplace name or a policy pin's attribution ahead of an admin layer (xai-grok-workspace/src/permission/managed_policy/layer.rs:16-25; mod.rs:42-62, :125, :188-263). The server decision is deny-wins: any deny blocks, then a managed-only lockdown requires a positive allow-entry grant, then every binding restricted source must allow (managed_policy/mcp.rs:353-366). Marketplace blocking happens at the add path, failing with a named error rather than silently skipping (xai-grok-pager/src/plugin_cmd.rs:875-880).
invariants: An unknown or non-inspectable MCP transport is restricted by EVERY entry, so a future transport variant cannot slip past a lockdown.
An ambiguous policy subject origin must classify as foreign, which is the fail-closed direction.
Name matching is exact equality after normalization, never substring, and an empty key never matches.
Grants are deliberately authority-blind while restrictions are not - the asymmetry is intentional and must not be smoothed away.
safety.failurePolicy: mixed but deny-biased - a layer whose config-to-JSON conversion fails is skipped and its pins are NOT applied, which is a genuine fail-open path on a malformed layer, while a dropped marketplace entry warns rather than silently allowing.

safety.name: external-auth-provider-and-api-key-lockout
safety.what: A deployment can replace the vendor's own authentication with an operator-supplied binary, and can lock out API-key authentication entirely. The provider is a command whose stdout carries the token, stderr the user-facing output and exit zero the success signal; the interactive path runs it with a five-minute timeout, while a headless mid-session refresh gets a much shorter budget (xai-grok-shell/src/auth/config.rs:64-66; src/auth/flow.rs:176-245; src/auth/external_auth.rs:42-44). The lockout knob `disable_api_key_auth` makes the API-key method neither advertised nor accepted, and the predicate ORs three independent sources - the config knob, the presence of a forced-login-team pin, and a call-time environment read - so a lower-trust user config cannot turn it back off (config.rs:74-77, :173-181). A login-principal check rejects a token whose team is not in the allowed set, and an empty allowed list fails closed (src/auth/oidc/protocol.rs:162-194).
invariants: A forced-login-team pin IMPLIES API-key auth is disabled, because team membership cannot be verified from a bare API key.
The client-side principal check is fail-fast UX and defence in depth, explicitly NOT the security boundary - the server re-validates the signed token, and the code says so.
The interactive provider run must not set the auth-expired environment variable, because operator binaries read it as 'headless, do not prompt'.
The lockout predicate must keep reading the environment at call time, or a long-lived process could miss an operator's change.
safety.failurePolicy: mixed - a provider that fails or times out returns nothing and the flow falls back rather than persisting a partial credential, while the principal check and the API-key kill switch are fail-closed.

safety.name: subscription-tier-and-zero-data-retention-gates
safety.what: Two server-derived account gates share one classifier each. The subscription tier arrives as a free-form display string, and a single shared function classifies the personal free tier and the basic X tier as restricted while treating everything else - INCLUDING unknown future tier names - as unrestricted; the function exists so the cosmetic command gate and the engine's capability and toolset gate cannot drift apart (xai-grok-shell/src/tier.rs:6-19). Zero-data-retention is a separate pair of flags: a team-level check matches two blocked-reason markers, and a data-collection check ORs the coding-data retention opt-out (src/auth/model.rs:169-181). The rendered block is the conjunction of zero-data-retention and the access flag being off, and zero-data-retention hard-blocks sharing outright (xai-grok-pager/src/app/app_view.rs:1240-1242; xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/share.rs:49-50).
invariants: The shell treats a MISSING tier as unrestricted (fail-open, because the server is the authority on per-tier limits) while the pager treats absence as restricted (cosmetic, and it recovers on the next settings update) - the two postures differ deliberately and the difference is documented at the classifier.
An unknown tier name must stay unrestricted, so a new server-side tier does not gate every user until the client is updated.
Zero-data-retention flags arrive through a background user merge and must survive a credential refresh.
safety.failurePolicy: mixed - fail-open on unknown tier names and fail-closed on the zero-data-retention gate, which blocks the session until the access flag is on.

constants.name: GROK_ZDR_ACCESS_ENABLED
constants.value: env override for the zero-data-retention access flag

safety.name: enterprise-proxy-ca-bundle
safety.what: Extra TLS roots for an enterprise proxy are opt-in through a dedicated environment variable with a fallback to the conventional certificate-file variable, and an explicitly EMPTY value disables both (xai-grok-extra-ca/src/lib.rs:14-18, :187-209). A bundle is read under a hard byte cap, PEM-parsed, and every certificate is X.509-validated through a throwaway root store before being added (lib.rs:275-326). Every client pins rustls with built-in webpki roots and the OS store enabled, and a default crypto provider is installed first-wins.
invariants: An explicitly empty value must disable the bundle, because the conventional certificate-file variable is frequently set process-wide by package managers and hermetic build tools - honoring it implicitly would silently change trust roots.
A bad bundle must never fail client construction; unparsable OS roots are likewise filtered so one bad root cannot break every client.
Every client must pin rustls, or feature unification can select a different TLS backend whose untyped errors break the certificate classifier.
safety.failurePolicy: fail-soft throughout - an unreadable, oversized, block-less or zero-certificate bundle warns and contributes zero extra roots while the client is still built.

model.name: embedded-default-model-catalogue
model.what: Default model ids are not string literals but a JSON file embedded with include_str! and parsed once into a LazyLock that asserts the declared `default` appears in `models` (xai-grok-models/src/lib.rs:10, :29-42). Four accessors expose the default plus `web_search`, `image_description` and `session_summary`, each falling back to `default` when its key is absent (lib.rs:45-68); the shipped file sets all four to grok-4.6 across exactly two entries (default_models.json:1-15). The same bytes are the catalogue source for the shell's richer per-model metadata: `default_models` re-parses DEFAULT_MODELS_JSON for context_window, api_backend, reasoning_efforts, variants and the compaction fields (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs:3707-3765). Default selection precedence is CLI > env `GROK_DEFAULT_MODEL` > config.toml > remote settings, implemented once in `resolve_string_flag` with the remote value as the weakest source (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs:827-847), and this embedded id is the last resort when no auth-visible selectable model exists (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/models/resolution.rs:85-88).
invariants: A `default` that is absent from `models` is a baked-in developer error and panics on first use rather than degrading to some fallback model (xai-grok-models/src/lib.rs:35-39).
The three task-specific accessors must keep falling back to `default`; returning nothing would make web-search, image-description and title-generation requests address no model.
The precedence ladder is load-bearing in one direction only: remote settings may supply a default but can never outrank CLI, env or config (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs:834-845).
model.failurePolicy: fail-closed at startup - malformed embedded JSON, a missing `models` array, an empty entry `model`, or a `default` absent from `models` all panic via expect/assert instead of silently running with a built-in id; once parsed, every accessor is total.

model.name: fail-closed-model-allowlist-and-visibility-gate
model.what: The model catalogue is filtered by one function in a fixed order: `disabled_models` are removed, then allowlist selectability is applied, then `hidden_models` are marked (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/models/resolution.rs:322-346). The allowlist has two authorities - a fleet pin taken from managed requirements, matched against the routing slug so a user-defined `[model.grok-4-anything]` cannot satisfy `grok-4*`, and a user `allowed_models` list matched against catalog key or slug (resolution.rs:205-218, :229-247, :293-297). A fail-closed pin, an unparsable glob, or a glob set matching nothing marks every entry non-selectable, and the user receives an administrator-policy message rather than a silent grant (resolution.rs:256-260, :278-286, :299-320). A second, orthogonal gate hides models by auth mode: `visible_for_auth(is_session_auth)` is false for `hidden` entries always and for entries with `supported_in_api = false` when the caller is API-key rather than session auth (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs:4274-4283). This is the model domain's enterprise/platform gate and it is implemented in the shell rather than in xai-grok-models: the embedded catalogue is only the candidate list, and the shell decides what a user may select or even see.
invariants: The order disabled -> allowed -> hidden is stated as the single source of truth for the catalog; a second filtering site would let the two disagree (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/models/resolution.rs:322).
A fleet pin matches the routing slug, never the user-chosen catalog key, so adding a local `[model.*]` alias cannot smuggle a denied model in (resolution.rs:293-297).
A fail-closed pin or an unparsable glob set must mark every entry non-selectable rather than falling back to unrestricted (resolution.rs:256-260, :278-286).
model.failurePolicy: fail-closed - an invalid pattern set or a fail-closed managed pin makes every model non-selectable, the catalog stays empty of selectable entries, and the denial is surfaced as policy text; nothing downgrades to unrestricted access.

constants.name: fleet vs user match target
constants.value: fleet: routing slug only; user: catalog key or slug

model.name: three-backend-sse-sampling-transport
model.what: One client speaks three wire shapes behind `ApiBackend`: ChatCompletions (`/v1/chat/completions`, the serde default), Responses (`/v1/responses`) and the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) (xai-grok-sampling-types/src/types.rs:989-999). Streaming is genuine SSE: the request sets `stream` true and `ACCEPT: text/event-stream`, the response byte stream is run through `eventsource()`, a leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped by hand because eventsource-stream 0.2.3 slices it at byte 1, `[DONE]` terminates, and the first transport error is surfaced once after which the scan terminates so a dead HTTP/2 connection cannot busy-loop (xai-grok-sampler/src/client.rs:1071-1129, :1316, :1363-1374). Every request carries x-grok-* correlation headers (conv, req, model-override, session, turn-index, transient-retry, agent, deployment, user) assembled in one place (client.rs:52-88). Layer 2 transforms the raw chunks of each backend into `SamplingEvent` streams (xai-grok-sampler/src/stream/mod.rs:1-15); the Responses decoder tolerates server tools `async_openai` cannot model by dropping the entries that fail to deserialize and re-parsing, and rewrites the terminal `total_tokens` from `context_details` (client.rs:90-120). A stream that stops producing is cut by an idle timeout, `DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS = 300` (xai-grok-sampler/src/actor/request_task.rs:41).
invariants: The BOM strip must stay: without it the first SSE frame of a BOM-prefixed response reaches the typed parser as garbage (xai-grok-sampler/src/client.rs:1071-1084).
A transport error must terminate the stream after being surfaced once; polling again after an h2 failure is the documented busy-loop (client.rs:1088-1096, :1126-1129).
A stream that ends without a terminal event is an explicit error, never an empty success (xai-grok-sampler/src/stream/collect.rs:16-21, :38-51).
model.failurePolicy: mixed - layers 1 and 2 surface typed errors as stream items (`SamplingError::EventStreamError`, `StreamError`, `Serialization`) and leave the decision to the retry loop above them; a stream with no terminal event fails closed with `SamplingErrorKind::Api`.

model.name: classified-retry-budget-with-pool-escape
model.what: Retry is a pure classifier plus an actor-side executor. `classify_error` returns Retry, RetryWithBackoff, RetryWithImageStrip, RetryWithClientRebuild, EmitToSession or Fatal (xai-grok-sampler/src/retry.rs:73-93): auth errors and encrypted-content errors are emitted to the session instead of retried; 413 and byte-size-coded rejections plus image-processing errors strip images and retry; a retry veto is Fatal because re-sending the same payload fails deterministically (xai-grok-sampling-types/src/error.rs:558-564); rate limits are capped at `min(max_retries, RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_THRESHOLD = 2)` and honour `Retry-After`, otherwise the budget is `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 15` overridable by `GROK_MAX_RETRIES` or a per-model `max_retries` (retry.rs:5-28, :130-143). Backoff is `2s << (n-1)` capped at `MAX_RETRY_BACKOFF = 30s` with +/-20% jitter; the FIRST transport retry is instead a 200 ms `TRANSPORT_REBUILD_BACKOFF` that rebuilds the client with `force_http1 = true` to escape a poisoned HTTP/2 pool (retry.rs:11-13, :42-64; xai-grok-sampler/src/actor/request_task.rs:453-474). A connection reset or broken pipe during body upload additionally strips images proactively before any retry, on the theory that a proxy rejected an oversized body without answering 413 (request_task.rs:363-388).
invariants: A retry veto must never be retried: the sampler actor and one-shot callers share `is_retry_vetoed` so a new veto lands everywhere at once (xai-grok-sampling-types/src/error.rs:558-564).
Only 401 is an auth error; 403 is a policy denial and must not trigger an OIDC refresh (xai-grok-sampling-types/src/error.rs:332-346).
The image-strip retry stops when nothing is left to strip, upgrading to Fatal instead of looping (xai-grok-sampler/src/actor/request_task.rs:411-418).
model.failurePolicy: mixed - transient errors retry under a bounded, jittered budget; deterministic classes fail fast as Fatal; auth failures are handed to the session for re-auth rather than retried; the HTTP/1.1 rebuild fails soft, reusing the old client if construction fails (xai-grok-sampler/src/actor/request_task.rs:469-474).

constants.name: GROK_MAX_RETRIES
constants.value: env override of the retry budget

model.name: shared-process-wide-sampling-clients-with-kill-switch
model.what: Sampling reuses two process-wide `reqwest::Client`s held in `OnceLock`s instead of building one per session: an HTTP/2 pooled client (h2 keepalive 15 s interval / 5 s timeout while idle, pool idle eviction after 90 s, `GROK_POOL_MAX_IDLE` default 2, `GROK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` default 10) and a pool-less HTTP/1.1 client used to escape a poisoned pool (xai-grok-sampler/src/shared_http.rs:14-15, :74-131). Sharing is safe only because the builders take no config-derived input - auth, extra headers, base URL and User-Agent are applied per request (shared_http.rs:1-9; xai-grok-sampler/src/client.rs:667+). Both clients are built through the TLS policy crate, which pins rustls (`use_rustls_tls`, native certs off, webpki bundle on), adds OS roots plus opt-in extra roots from `GROK_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` (fallback `SSL_CERT_FILE`, bundle capped at 1 MiB) and reads the roots once per process (xai-grok-extra-ca/src/lib.rs:14-18, :47-59, :82-101). Two kill switches exist: `GROK_SAMPLER_SHARED_CLIENT=0|false` builds a fresh client per `SamplingClient`, and `SamplerConfig::force_http1` selects the HTTP/1.1 client directly (shared_http.rs:17-32; client.rs:612-617). A failed build is deliberately not cached, so the cell stays empty and the next call retries (shared_http.rs:34-50).
invariants: The shared builders must stay configuration-free: any config-derived input (auth, headers, base URL) belongs per request, or two sessions would share another session's credentials (shared_http.rs:1-9).

A build failure must not populate the OnceLock; caching it would make one transient failure permanent for the process (shared_http.rs:34-50, pinned by the `shared_does_not_cache_build_failures` test).
Every client must be built through the TLS policy helper, because rustls must stay pinned; a native-tls client would break the certificate-error classifier (xai-grok-extra-ca/src/lib.rs:4, :47-59).
model.failurePolicy: fail-soft - client construction errors are returned as `SamplingError::Http` to the caller and are not latched; a bad extra CA bundle is logged and skipped rather than failing client construction (xai-grok-extra-ca/src/lib.rs:1-4).

constants.name: h2 keepalive
constants.value: interval 15 s, timeout 5 s, while_idle true

model.name: origin-scoped-transport-prewarm
model.what: Transport warm-up is best effort and credential-free: `prewarm_transport` dials the endpoint origin once per pool-idle window through the shared pooled client, carries no credentials, drains the body up to a 64 KiB cap and is bounded by a 15 s timeout (xai-grok-sampler/src/prewarm.rs:1-16, :63-128, :194-216). Concurrency is controlled by an origin claim state machine - an origin is `InFlight` or `Warmed(Instant)`, a claim is released by `Drop` unless committed, so every non-warmed outcome (failure, timeout, cap) frees the origin for a later dial (prewarm.rs:130-158). At most 32 origins are tracked, with a sweep of stale entries before a full tracker rejects the prewarm (prewarm.rs:16, :160-187). Because reqwest exposes no pool-hit signal, the crate records freshness at first sampling use - `warm_fresh`, `warm_stale`, `warm_pending`, `warm_absent` - into the `sampler.transport_prewarm_first_use` span (prewarm.rs:260-323).
invariants: A prewarm must carry no credentials; it is a bare GET of the origin (prewarm.rs:1-4, :199).
A claim must be released on every path that did not warm, or a failed prewarm would permanently suppress later attempts for that origin (prewarm.rs:144-150).
The tracker is bounded at 32 origins and sweeps expired entries before reporting full, so one noisy process cannot grow it without limit (prewarm.rs:16, :160-170).
model.failurePolicy: fail-open - prewarming is skipped on every adverse outcome (`NoOrigin`, `ClientUnavailable`, `AlreadyClaimed`, `TrackerFull`, `Failed`, `TimedOut`) and a skipped prewarm never fails the sampling request; only a fully drained pooled response counts as warmed.

model.name: refresh-aware-credential-seam-with-401-attribution
model.what: Credentials for every outbound data-collector and sampler request go through one dependency-inversion seam: `HttpAuth::apply` builds the header and `AuthCredentialProvider` adds a refresh-aware snapshot plus 401 recovery (xai-grok-auth/src/auth_provider.rs:29-57). The snapshot is a structured value (token, user, team, deployment, api_key_id, organization) rather than a bare string, because the OTel layer and 401 attribution need identity fields (auth_provider.rs:9-27). The production implementation checks wire validity before returning a token and delegates 401 recovery to the auth manager's background recovery path (xai-grok-shell/src/auth/credential_provider.rs:79-117); a static provider reports `refresh_after_unauthorized() == false` so no refresh is attempted (auth_provider.rs:91-102). The optional `middleware` feature supplies `AuthRetryMiddleware`, which stamps the bearer, clones the request, and on 401 refreshes and replays up to `max_retries` times (xai-grok-auth/src/retry_middleware.rs:65-98); the feature is enabled by xai-grok-http, xai-file-utils and xai-grok-shell (xai-grok-auth/Cargo.toml:10; xai-grok-http/Cargo.toml:15). Attribution reads a `StampedBearerSuffix` recorded in the request extensions at stamp time - only the last 12 characters of the token, counted as chars because `auth.json` or an auth-provider command can return non-ASCII - rather than re-resolving the token, which would race the refresh the 401 itself triggers (retry_middleware.rs:12-28, :44-55; xai-grok-auth/src/bearer_fragment.rs:4-15). The refresh lifetime is also protected across suspend: `xai-system-power` exists so an AuthManager can avoid starting a refresh just before sleep and may block a `WillSleep` handler briefly to let an in-flight rotation finish (xai-system-power/src/lib.rs:1-14, :38-59).
invariants: `snapshot().token` must mirror the bearer `HttpAuth::apply` would send, or 401-attribution prefixes will not match the request that was actually made (xai-grok-auth/src/auth_provider.rs:35-38).
Only the bearer tail is stamped and logged: JWT heads are a shared constant and the tail is the safe part for a sink (retry_middleware.rs:12-16).
The suffix must be taken by char index, not byte offset, or a multi-byte token panics (bearer_fragment.rs:8-14).
model.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a header that cannot be built is warned about and the request continues unauthenticated (retry_middleware.rs:51-54); a refresh failure simply ends the retry loop and returns the last 401 response (retry_middleware.rs:80-97); a deployment key never refreshes and never sends the token-auth header (xai-grok-shell/src/auth/credential_provider.rs:106-116).
