model.name: secret-redaction-before-log-and-sink
model.what: One crate owns redaction for everything that leaves the process. `redact_secrets` runs a `RegexSet` prefilter and returns the input borrowed when nothing matches, then applies ten ordered passes: PEM private-key blocks, `sk-`/`sk_`/`xai-` keys, AWS AKIA/ASIA ids, GitHub PATs, GitLab/Slack tokens, Google `AIza` keys, `Bearer` tokens, bare JWTs, URLs (userinfo, fragment and sensitive query keys such as access_token/api_key/code/state stripped) and a generic `secret|token|password = value` assignment pattern with an 8-character value floor (xai-grok-secrets/src/sanitizer.rs:5-51, :53-70, :75-108, :278-304). `redact_user_paths` collapses `$HOME` to `~` and whole path segments equal to the OS username to `<user>`, with a `/Users|/home` regex backstop used only when the environment carries no home or username, so REST paths like `/users/<id>` are not mangled (sanitizer.rs:143-200). `walk_json_strings`/`redact_json_string_values` apply the same scrub to every string value of a JSON document, and are the entry points used by the telemetry exporter, the Sentry path and the Mixpanel client (sanitizer.rs:110-126; xai-grok-telemetry/src/redact_common.rs:13-14, xai-grok-telemetry/src/sentry.rs:94, xai-mixpanel/src/lib.rs:55).
invariants: The `\b` anchor on the API-key pattern is load-bearing: without it `task-`, `disk-` and `risk-` prefixes turn into redactions (xai-grok-secrets/src/sanitizer.rs:8-11).
The username backstop runs only when `$HOME`/`$USER` are unavailable, because regex-based user matching over-redacts real paths (sanitizer.rs:190-195).
`redact_url` must rebuild the query through the form-urlencoded serializer so the `redacted` placeholder is not percent-encoded (sanitizer.rs:277-304).
model.failurePolicy: fail-open with respect to flow (redaction never errors and never blocks a request) but fail-safe in the direction that matters: an unmatched string is passed through unchanged, so the regexes are the only defence and a new secret shape requires a new pattern.

extension.name: mcp-multi-transport-with-in-process-acp-bridge
extension.what: MCP is served over three transports, one of which avoids IPC entirely. The shipped set is an rmcp HTTP/SSE streamable client transport, a stdio child process transport with spawn-guard and process-group teardown, and a zero-IPC bridge typed as `AsyncRwTransport<RoleClient, DuplexStream, DuplexStream>` that tunnels each MCP JSON-RPC message to the SDK host as the ACP reverse request `x.ai/mcp/sdk_call` (xai-grok-mcp/src/acp_transport.rs:44; xai-grok-mcp/src/wire.rs:10-33). `start_mcp_server` builds one client per configured server, and the init state machine deliberately returns control to the session BEFORE per-server handshakes drain, tracking progress through a NotStarted/Starting/Finished state plus a handshaking set (xai-grok-mcp/src/servers.rs:248, :2577). A resilient transport wrapper decode-tolerates garbage stdio lines.
invariants: reqwest 0.13 is a private implementation detail of the servers module and is deliberately NOT re-exported, because the rest of the workspace is pinned to reqwest 0.12 and a re-export would collide.
The client event sender is private so callers must go through the setter, which fans the sender into already-owned clients; assigning the field directly would strand existing clients.
The ACP bridge is declared HALF-DUPLEX: server-to-client traffic (notifications, sampling/createMessage, roots/list) is not bridged, and elicitation is not advertised on it.
extension.failurePolicy: mixed - a bridge reverse-call failure is fail-closed by design (a missing tool server is a real error), while a serve failure records an init-failed marker and surfaces the server as unavailable rather than aborting the session.

extension.name: mcp-liveness-probe-and-token-fenced-retry
extension.what: MCP clients are watched by polling rather than by a shutdown future, and retries are fenced by an attempt token. Each successful handshake arms a one-shot poller ticking every 500 ms calling `liveness_check()`; on the FIRST transport-closed observation while the client is Ready it emits exactly one transport-closed event and exits, and on a transient (state drifted out of Ready) it withdraws silently (xai-grok-mcp/src/liveness.rs:53, :121-180). The task clears its own liveness slot before exiting so a later arm can re-establish it, and client removal calls a cancel-watcher for the same reason. Separately, a spawn that fails for connectivity rather than auth records an unreachable marker and schedules a respawn after a cooldown; `take_unreachable_retry_candidates` moves a due server from Cooling to InFlight with a monotonic token, and the attempt must present that token to settle, so stale tokens no-op (xai-grok-mcp/src/servers.rs:856-896, :949). A separate attempt lease reclaims an InFlight entry whose future was cancelled mid-await and can therefore never settle.
invariants: Polling is a consequence of the quarantined rmcp build: the running service exposes no shutdown future, so the only signal is a transport-closed predicate - replacing polling with a select would require patching rmcp itself.
A watcher must never emit on a non-Ready state, because resetting the transport moves state out of Ready and a naive check would report a false transport-closed.
The attempt token is the attempt's proof of ownership: no settle path may skip the check, or a cancelled attempt could install a client over a newer one.
Config teardown must invalidate the token, or a removed server's retry could resurrect it.
An in-flight server is never handed to another trigger, so retry triggers cannot dogpile the discovery and probe budget.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft throughout - a send failure during teardown logs at debug and exits without retry, non-Ready states exit silently, and an unreachable server degrades to unavailable with a scheduled retry rather than to permanent tool loss.

extension.name: mcp-oauth-consent-with-in-and-cross-process-dedup
extension.what: HTTP MCP servers that advertise OAuth run a browser consent flow, deduplicated at two levels so a second trigger cannot open a second browser. In-process callers are deduped through a static in-flight map of server name to a watch receiver plus a generation counter; cross-process callers are deduped through an fs2 lock under the grok home, and a second process polls the credential store instead of re-authenticating (xai-grok-mcp/src/oauth.rs:15-24, :61, :224). Credentials live in `mcp_credentials.json` under the grok home behind an owner-only atomic-write store, and a disk-only classifier decides stored-credentials versus needs-login versus unknown WITHOUT a network round trip (xai-grok-mcp/src/auth_status.rs:42; xai-grok-mcp/src/credentials.rs:60).
invariants: A stored entry with NO token response is an UNFINISHED login (needs-login), while an expired token that still has a refresh token classifies as stored - the distinction is what stops a half-completed consent from reading as success.
On the disk path the observed token is seeded into the freshness record, so a re-authentication cannot read the same token back and treat it as fresh.
The agent-id routing header is stripped from every caller-supplied HTTP/SSE config and re-added only by the spawn context - it is an advisory routing hint and never an authentication.
Discovery must map a legacy-endpoint fallback onto 'no authorization support' rather than attempting a legacy flow.
extension.failurePolicy: mixed but scoped - a failure to construct the auth manager degrades to no-OAuth-support and falls through to the anonymous path (which is separately probed), while a hung authorization server is timeout-bounded rather than wedging the manager lock.

extension.name: mcp-elicitation-single-slot-rendezvous
extension.what: Server-initiated `elicitation/create` is forwarded to the client as the ACP request `x.ai/mcp/elicit`, with completion notified as `x.ai/mcp/elicit_complete` (xai-grok-mcp/src/wire.rs:28). The inbox is a single-slot rendezvous - a mutex-guarded optional job plus a notify - where push REPLACES any previous job, close cancels the outstanding one, and receive returns nothing once closed (xai-grok-mcp/src/elicitation.rs:63, :108). Message size, URL length, id length and schema bytes are all validated AT INGEST against caps defined in the tools crate, so a consumer never observes an unsupported mode or an oversized schema (xai-grok-mcp/src/elicitation.rs:178-181; xai-grok-tools/src/mcp_elicitation/schema.rs:9-17).
invariants: Only one elicitation can be outstanding by construction, and a second REPLACES the first while also answering the displaced one with a cancel result - replacing without answering would strand the server.
Size and charset validation happens before enqueue, not at consumption.
On an unsupported mode the bridge must DECLINE rather than error, because the MCP server needs a valid result either way.
The bridge is not advertised on the zero-IPC ACP transport, so a compliant in-process server never sends elicitation there.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft and closed toward the server, never toward the user - an unsupported mode declines, a missing bridge declines, a closed channel cancels, and a dropped oneshot cancels.

extension.name: mcp-tool-name-and-icon-ingest-hardening
extension.what: Everything an MCP server advertises is validated at ingest against the strictest common denominator. Every tool name from `tools/list` passes a validator against `TOOL_NAME_REGEX = ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}$`, which is the intersection of the Anthropic/OpenAI form and the Gemini form (xai-grok-mcp/src/servers.rs:82-86). Protocol icons ingest through a typed wrapper with INDEPENDENT caps on count, source bytes including data URIs, mime-type bytes, size tokens and token bytes, and an unknown theme deserializes to an explicit unknown variant rather than failing the whole server (servers.rs:100-127).
invariants: The name regex must stay at the strictest provider intersection - loosening it to Gemini's dotted form would break Anthropic and OpenAI, so the constraint is about what the DOWNSTREAM providers accept, not about MCP.
Icon caps are applied at ingest and must not be re-expanded by a later consumer.
An unknown icon theme must degrade to a variant rather than failing the server, so a future theme cannot take a whole MCP server offline.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on an invalid tool name (that tool is rejected) and fail-soft on icons (oversized or unknown entries are dropped while the server still loads).

extension.name: language-server-client-with-inert-by-default-backend
extension.what: A real LSP client ships: roughly eighteen files spawn language-server processes with piped stdio, run an async-lsp client main loop, perform the initialize handshake with a declared capability set, and issue real text-document traffic - go-to-definition, find-references, hover, go-to-implementation, document symbols, workspace symbols, publish-diagnostics notifications and pull-model diagnostics - with one client per server orchestrated by a manager (xai-grok-tools/src/implementations/lsp/client.rs:221, :431; src/implementations/lsp/config.rs:33). The model reaches it through a first-class `lsp` tool whose backend is injected only when at least one language server is configured from the grok home or workspace config plus plugin-provided servers. Project-scoped server config passes through an untrusted-project filter.
invariants: The `lsp` tool is registered in the default toolset but its BACKEND is inert until a server is configured - a tool that exists while its manager does not is the intended shape, so presence in the toolset is not evidence the capability is live.
Project-scoped language-server configuration must keep passing through the untrusted-project filter, or an untrusted checkout could launch an arbitrary server binary.
The LSP path is distinct from the tree-sitter code-navigation path: the ACP `x.ai/code/*` navigation methods route to the tree-sitter index, not to a language server.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a server crash, retry or startup is surfaced as a telemetry event and the tool returns error text, and diagnostics use short bounded waits rather than blocking a turn.
extension.wiringNote: The dependency is `async-lsp` 0.2.3; tower-lsp and lsp-server are absent. Do not conflate this with xai-codebase-graph: the ACP methods `x.ai/code/goto-definition`, `goto-references`, `find-definitions` and `find-references` (xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/code_nav.rs:178-265) route to the tree-sitter index.

extension.name: skill-discovery-with-ignore-versus-disabled
extension.what: Skills are `SKILL.md` files discovered from a precedence-ordered directory set - cwd, then a git-root walk trying each vendor rules directory (gated by a compat config), an optional workspace-user directory, the global grok home plus other agents' homes, configured extra paths, launcher-injected server directories and finally bundled directories at lowest priority (xai-grok-agent/src/prompt/skills.rs:21, :64, :138). The model sees them two ways: a static listing inside the skill tool's description for on-demand loading, and eager injection for an agent definition's declared skills. Discovery walks recursively to a depth limit and parses frontmatter with byte caps.
invariants: `[skills].ignore` and `[skills].disabled` are DIFFERENT states and must stay so: ignore hides a skill entirely while disabled keeps it listed but unloadable and out of the system prompt.
A higher-priority source overrides a same-named lower one, and a plugin skill survives a bare-name collision under a qualified name.
Skill discovery deliberately does NOT honor gitignore for skill roots, unlike instruction-file discovery which does - the two traversals have different rules on purpose.
A skill name must satisfy a lowercase-letters-numbers-hyphens validator within a maximum length.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft - an unreadable or over-cap SKILL.md is skipped, an over-long description is capped rather than rejected, and a body that cannot be read falls back to frontmatter-only metadata.
extension.wiringNote: There is NO `[skills] enabled` flag - the feature is always on, and the config surface is paths, ignore, disabled, server directories and bundled directories only. Live mid-session rediscovery comes from a file watcher over the skills, commands and workflow directories (xai-grok-shell/src/config/watcher.rs:476).

extension.name: plugin-marketplace-install-with-tighten-only-sha-pinning
extension.what: A marketplace catalogue layers over an existing install-registry pipeline. Sources come from configured marketplace entries (a local path, or a git URL with an optional branch) plus vendor-compat settings files; git sources are cloned shallowly into a persistent cache under a hash of the URL, behind an fs2 file lock with a TTL consumed through an RAII lease (xai-grok-plugin-marketplace/src/config.rs:34; src/git.rs:16-20, :240). The official source is auto-registered once on first run behind a flag. Installs route either through a local copy from the synced checkout or through a remote clone pinned to a `git_sha` when the index provides one, and the host exposes the surface over ACP list and action methods (xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/marketplace.rs:20).
invariants: Plugins are NOT cryptographically signed, and an unpinned remote install tracks a mutable ref - publishing a sha in the plugin index is the documented mitigation, so `require_sha` is a policy control rather than a verification control.
`require_sha` is TIGHTEN-ONLY: config or environment can turn it on and neither can turn it off, so a user-writable layer cannot weaken an admin's pin.
`require_sha` covers every remote-fetch path but NOT plugins vendored inside a marketplace source checkout - the gap is structural, not an oversight to be assumed away.
The official-source comparison must normalize case, a leading www, trailing slashes and .git, and the HTTPS/SSH/scp URL forms before matching.
extension.failurePolicy: mixed - `require_sha` fails an unpinned remote install closed, a hung git network operation is killed at a timeout and reported, and a malformed marketplace source entry warns and is skipped while the rest of the file still parses.
extension.wiringNote: Adding a source is additionally gated by the managed-settings marketplace allowlist: when restricted, a non-matching identity is a validation error and local paths never match a git-URL allowlist so they are blocked - intentionally fail-closed (xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/marketplace.rs:825-835). A URL is also probed with a timed `git ls-remote` before being persisted (git.rs:250). `require_sha` defaults OFF, with the stated reason that existing unpinned catalogs keep installing.

extension.name: workflow-rhai-engine-with-journal-replay
extension.what: Workflows are Rhai scripts executed against a host-function surface of agent, parallel and the complete/pause/emit family, and every host call is content-hashed and appended to an append-only journal keyed by a dense sequence number (xai-workflow/src/engine.rs:492, :511; src/journal.rs:39). A re-run REPLAYS recorded results instead of re-spawning agents, and a hash mismatch raises a divergence error stating that the script is nondeterministic or was edited mid-run. The outcome type admits Completed, Paused with a reason, BudgetExceeded, Cancelled and Failed, with pause reasons distinguishing user, back-off, no-progress, verification and infra (xai-workflow/src/run.rs:5).
invariants: The journal must be dense and bounded BEFORE restore: loading rejects a restore whose size or entry count would exceed the cap, so a run can never be written into an unresumable state.
Replay must stay deterministic - host-call order and hash ARE the identity, so a mid-run script edit is a fatal divergence rather than a silent re-execution.
Parallel items must be option maps.
Terminal outcomes must never be demoted by a later event.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on journal integrity (an unsafe restore, a sequence gap or a divergence all abort the run) and fail-soft on a live host call, which is recorded as a sentinel so a resume can retry it.
extension.wiringNote: Wired and DEFAULT-ON: the resolver defaults true and the env var, config key and remote setting are kill-switches only (xai-grok-shell/src/agent/config.rs:2689-2702).

extension.name: subagent-bundle-cache-with-user-edit-preservation
extension.what: The published subagent bundle - personas, roles, agents, skills and workflows - is cached on disk under the grok home with a manifest that records a checksum for every file the crate writes, so a file the user edited by hand is never overwritten and never pruned (xai-grok-bundle/src/lib.rs:1-6). Archive extraction is bounded on three axes - entry count, per-entry size and total decompressed size - and every path is sanitized before it is joined onto the cache root.
invariants: The checksum manifest is what makes hand-editing safe: without it a bundle refresh would either clobber user edits or prune them as unknown files.
Extraction bounds must cover the total decompressed size, not only per-entry size, or a many-entry archive bypasses the cap.
Path sanitization must happen BEFORE the join onto the cache root, so a traversal entry cannot escape.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on an unsafe archive (extraction is bounded and paths are sanitized) and fail-soft on a user-edited file (preserved rather than overwritten or pruned).

service.name: double-fork-daemonize-with-single-instance-pidfile-lock
service.what: On Unix `daemonize()` runs `fork_and_exit_parent()` (the parent exits 0), `setsid()`, a second fork, `chdir("/")`, then redirects stdin to `/dev/null` and stdout/stderr onto an append-mode log; on Windows there is no fork, only stdio repointing at the log handle (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/daemonize.rs:142-167, :169-198). Single-instance exclusion is an advisory `flock` held for the daemon's whole life by `PidFile::_file`, and the PID text stored in the file is explicitly advisory for diagnostics - exclusion comes from the lock, not the number (daemonize.rs:270-307). `acquire_or_take_over` escalates against a live predecessor: read the recorded PID, signal it gracefully, poll the lock for `TAKEOVER_GRACE`, then kill forcefully and poll for `TAKEOVER_KILL_GRACE`, declining if a newer spawn won the lock instead (daemonize.rs:309-360). Every daemon-owned file - log, pidfile and the preview-proxy log - is opened through one helper that adds `O_NOFOLLOW` and mode 0600 (daemonize.rs:220-229). The binary calls this only under `--daemonize`, which defaults off (xai-grok-workspace/src/bin/workspace_server.rs:246-260, :842-845).
invariants: The double-fork and `setsid()` must run before anything starts threads: the binary daemonizes before it builds the tokio runtime (xai-grok-workspace/src/bin/workspace_server.rs:246-260, :278).

The flock is never bypassed - a guard exists only while the lock is held, and a contended acquire returns `Ok(None)` so the caller exits quietly instead of running a second instance (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/daemonize.rs:280-307, :356-359).
Daemon-owned files must keep `O_NOFOLLOW` plus 0600; the helper is shared with the preview proxy so both files stay equally strict (daemonize.rs:220-229).
service.failurePolicy: mixed - exclusivity fails closed (a held lock means the new process declines and exits), while OOM protection fails soft: a failed `oom_score_adj` write is logged and reported as false but the server still starts (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/daemonize.rs:110-139, :65-68).

service.name: preview-proxy-supervision-with-loopback-activity-scraping
service.what: After the workspace server daemonizes, the supervisor execs exactly one child, `/usr/local/bin/xai-grok-preview-proxy`, capturing its stdout/stderr into a workspace-server-owned log that is served back through the diagnostics endpoints (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/preview_supervisor.rs:26-31). The child is spawned with `kill_on_drop(true)` inside a restart loop whose base delay doubles up to a cap, and a run lasting at least `PREVIEW_PROXY_HEALTHY_RUN_SECS` resets the backoff step so a crash loop pins at the cap instead of growing (preview_supervisor.rs:33-40, :166-188, :307-341). On Linux a `pre_exec` sets `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG(SIGKILL)` and re-checks `getppid()` to close the fork/exec race, because PDEATHSIG keys off the spawning thread and the task must therefore run on long-lived runtime workers (preview_supervisor.rs:10-13, :281). Two scrapers then poll the proxy's loopback control endpoints: `/__control/activity` feeds a sink that withholds idle (preview_supervisor.rs:401-435, :523-585) and `/__control/metrics` is exported to the hub metrics sink under the `preview_proxy_` prefix every 60 s (preview_supervisor.rs:618-637). The whole supervisor is gated: it is spawned only when `--preview-enabled` was passed, which defaults off (xai-grok-workspace/src/bin/workspace_server.rs:193, :433-439, :903).
invariants: The child is spawned only after daemonize, so it inherits the daemon's session and process group and escapes the launcher's process-group reap (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/preview_supervisor.rs:6-9).
The supervise task must run on long-lived worker threads: PDEATHSIG keys off the spawning thread, so a short-lived thread would kill the child spuriously (preview_supervisor.rs:11-13).
A healthy run resets the restart step, so a crash loop converges on a fixed interval rather than an unbounded delay (preview_supervisor.rs:33-40).
service.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a spawn or log-open failure backs off and retries rather than dropping the task; an unreachable proxy or a bad scrape body is a quiet no-op on the activity path and a logged debug on the metrics path (xai-grok-workspace-daemon/src/preview_supervisor.rs:539-637).

constants.name: PREVIEW_PROXY_HEALTHY_RUN_SECS / RESTART_BACKOFF_BASE / CAP
constants.value: 30 s healthy run; backoff 1 s doubling to a 30 s cap

service.name: loopback-diagnostics-readiness-server
service.what: An in-guest HTTP server answers three unauthenticated GET routes for the standalone workspace server: `/ready`, `/statusz` and `/logs` (xai-grok-diag-server/src/lib.rs:1-5, :371-393). It binds either a Unix socket, removing any stale file first and then `set_permissions(0o600)`, or loopback TCP on `Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST`, and it never goes through the sandbox port mapping (lib.rs:398-449). `/ready` is 200 only when the hub state is `Connected` and 503 otherwise, with the body served either way so naive HTTP probes and state parsers agree; `/statusz` flattens those fields and adds `os` plus advisory `image_capabilities`; `/logs` tails the daemon log with a 64 KiB default clamped to a 256 KiB hard cap, returns 404 when there is no log file, and answers a generic 500 body on I/O error so the log path is never echoed (lib.rs:64-97, :333-358, :377-385). State is a mutex latch with deliberate stickiness: `set_failed` is terminal, `set_terminal_close` latches a hub close code (4100-4199) that `set_disconnected` must not clear, and `revive_connected` clears it only for a code in the caller's allow-list (lib.rs:149-231). Not gated by a flag - the workspace server always starts it and advertises `diag: true` in its capability manifest (xai-grok-workspace/src/bin/workspace_server.rs:231); the TCP listener exists only on Windows, so `DEFAULT_DIAG_PORT` is inert on Unix (workspace_server.rs:408-411).
invariants: The `/ready` field set is a frozen contract with the sandbox readiness gate: never rename or remove fields, additions only (xai-grok-diag-server/src/lib.rs:67-68).
`/ready` must never be 2xx while the state is not `Connected`, or a probe would disagree with a client parsing `state` (lib.rs:377-385).
`image_capabilities` is advisory only and never an authorization input, because the guest can forge the markers (lib.rs:92-97).
service.failurePolicy: mixed - a bind failure is fatal only on the daemonized path, which has a grep-able marker and a dedicated exit code, and is warn-only otherwise (xai-grok-diag-server/src/lib.rs:33-37; xai-grok-workspace/src/bin/workspace_server.rs:408-431); socket `chmod` failure is warn-only, and `/logs` read errors return a generic 500 body.
service.wiringNote: moduleCoverage files this crate as "Service-domain", so it is recorded here rather than under `ops` where the brief's starting list placed it. Its inputs are the workspace daemon's own log path and the hub connection state, both owned by the workspace server binary.

service.name: shared-http-clients-with-poison-pool-escape
service.what: Shared `reqwest` client construction with one escape hatch. `shared_client()` is an HTTP/2 client with keepalive, a 30 s pool idle timeout and a mode header; `shared_upload_client()` is HTTP/1.1-only with `pool_max_idle_per_host(2)` and a 10 s idle timeout because a degraded multiplexed connection silently drops multipart bodies; `shared_startup_blocking_client()` carries `STARTUP_FETCH_TIMEOUT` as both connect and read ceiling; and `fresh_http1_client()` is a pool-less, never-cached client used to escape a poisoned pool (xai-grok-http/src/lib.rs:256-269, :285-298, :326-334, :346-350, :557-576). `send_with_retry_escaping_pool` runs early attempts on the pooled client and swaps the final attempt of a multi-attempt run onto the pool-less client, so a tight-budget caller escapes a reset or GOAWAY connection immediately instead of waiting for pool eviction (lib.rs:501-527). Transport failures are classified by descending the cause chain, with certificate verdicts separated from plain connect failures (lib.rs:404-449). Two compile-time asserts pin the budget relationships between the startup timeouts (lib.rs:37-49). moduleCoverage calls this crate "infrastructure ... contributes no mechanism of its own"; the pool-escape policy plus the failure classifier are the mechanism, and the file's own `hintCorrections` assigns the crate to `service`.
invariants: The pool escape must stay on the LAST attempt: moving it earlier makes every retry pay a fresh connection setup (xai-grok-http/src/lib.rs:501-527).

The two compile-time asserts must keep holding - `SETTINGS_REAPPLY_TIMEOUT > STARTUP_FETCH_TIMEOUT * (1 + SETTINGS_FETCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS)` and `MIN_CLIENT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT >= 2 * STARTUP_AUTH_TIMEOUT` (lib.rs:37-49).
Certificate trust failures must be classified before the generic connect case, or an untrusted issuer reads as an unreachable host (lib.rs:404-449).
service.failurePolicy: mixed - retry count and retryability are owned by the caller and the helper returns a classified transport error rather than inventing an outcome; the pool-escape attempt is best effort and its failure is classified like any other attempt (xai-grok-http/src/lib.rs:404-449, :501-527).

constants.name: shared client pool knobs
constants.value: pool_idle_timeout 30 s (HTTP/2); upload client idle 10 s with max 2 idle per host

service.name: acp-gateway-channel-pair-and-fire-and-forget-notifications
service.what: The ACP transport is a pair of linked unbounded mpsc channels with a oneshot response slot per request: `acp_channels()` builds the pair and `acp_send` attaches the responder, awaits the reply, and maps a closed channel to a typed error (xai-acp-lib/src/channel.rs:28-40). `acp_gateway` builds the sender/receiver pair, and the receiver's `run` loop dispatches every message through the `handle!` macro, which builds an optional span from `_meta` and spawns the handler on an injected spawn function so the loop never blocks on a handler (xai-acp-lib/src/gateway.rs:99, :144-174). The sender offers `forward_with_completion` and `forward_fire_and_forget`, and both `session_notification` and `ext_notification` are deliberately fire-and-forget because blocking on a degraded relay can stall a session (gateway.rs:455, :468). Channel failures carry a typed discriminant in the error `data` - `xaiAcpChannelFailure` with `send_failed` / `recv_failed` - so "the receiver was already gone" is distinguishable from "a peer took the request then vanished" without substring-matching the message (xai-acp-lib/src/common.rs:41-67).
invariants: The channel-failure discriminant must stay a typed field in the error `data`, never be inferred from message text (xai-acp-lib/src/common.rs:41-67).
Per-message tracing spans are opt-in (`tracing: bool`, `with_tracing`) and off by default (xai-acp-lib/src/gateway.rs:25, :43, :93).
The default dispatcher is `tokio::task::spawn_local`, so a receiver needs a `LocalSet` unless `with_spawn_fn` overrides it (gateway.rs:36-37, :50-56).
service.failurePolicy: fail-soft - a dropped receiver discards the message rather than failing the caller, `acp_send` surfaces a typed `INTERNAL_ERROR` carrying the discriminant, and handler work is isolated in its spawned task (xai-acp-lib/src/common.rs:41-67).

service.name: acp-stdio-line-transport-hardening
service.what: The stdin side of the ACP wire is read by a dedicated OS thread doing blocking reads into a depth-64 channel with `blocking_send`, which gives natural backpressure instead of buffering without bound (xai-acp-lib/src/stdin_reader.rs:56-79, :122). On Windows an `isolate_process_stdin` helper exists beside that reader so the process-wide stdin handle can be handled separately from the reader's own handle (stdin_reader.rs:87-93, :136-137). Every line then passes through `normalize_json_line`, which rewrites only lines containing a `\/` escape that the pinned acp envelope would otherwise drop, and forwards lines that already parse as `RawIncomingMessage` byte-identical (xai-acp-lib/src/normalize.rs:15-45). `LineBufferedRead` pre-reads whole newline-delimited lines on a task and serves them from a channel so `poll_read` returns `Pending` only between lines, which is what makes it usable inside a biased select, with a per-line ceiling of `MAX_LINE_SIZE` (xai-acp-lib/src/line_reader.rs:30, :51-54, :163-168).
invariants: Normalization must stay limited to the one escape that breaks the pinned envelope: valid lines are forwarded byte-identical and unparseable input passes through untouched, leaving garbage handling to the acp crate (xai-acp-lib/src/normalize.rs:38-45).
A line larger than `MAX_LINE_SIZE` must be an `InvalidData` error, not unbounded buffering (xai-acp-lib/src/line_reader.rs:163-168).
The stdin reader thread must park on a full channel rather than dropping or growing, which is what `blocking_send` on a depth-64 channel provides (xai-acp-lib/src/stdin_reader.rs:56, :122).
service.failurePolicy: fail-soft - EOF or a read error closes the channel, an over-long line is a typed error rather than memory growth, and anything the normalizer cannot parse is forwarded unchanged (xai-acp-lib/src/stdin_reader.rs:122; src/line_reader.rs:163-168).

service.name: streaming-stt-dictation-with-out-of-process-mic-capture
service.what: Voice input is a streaming STT client plus a pipeline task, not a renderer concern: `run_voice_pipeline` consumes press/release/shutdown commands and drives a session that connects to the STT websocket, sends binary PCM and then `{"type":"audio.done"}`, and maps server events into Created/Partial/Done/Error (xai-grok-voice/src/pipeline.rs:37, :241-249; xai-grok-voice/src/stt/streaming.rs:66-88). Two bounds keep it honest: a `NO_SPEECH_TIMEOUT` watchdog tears down a silent session with microphone guidance instead of streaming a dead input, and a `BACKLOG_MAX_CHUNKS` backlog bridges capture to the socket so capture never backpressures during the handshake (pipeline.rs:133-153, :181-183, :249). Capture is deliberately out of process where the audio stack is expensive: the binary re-execs itself as a hidden `__mic-capture` helper that speaks a one-line READY handshake, Linux falls back to system recorders probed with a short `--raw` check, and the feature is compile-time gated by the `audio` cargo feature (xai-grok-voice/src/lib.rs:42-52, :81-84; xai-grok-voice/src/audio/capture_subprocess.rs:28-33, :73, :161; xai-grok-voice/src/audio/capture_linux.rs:31-39, :164). Audio defaults to 16 kHz with `stt_ws_path` `/v1/stt` (xai-grok-voice/src/config.rs:6, :37).
invariants: The microphone must be stopped before end-of-utterance is signalled, so no stray PCM is queued after `audio.done` (xai-grok-voice/src/pipeline.rs:241).
A session that produces no speech must end in an explicit error rather than an open microphone (pipeline.rs:181-183, :249).
The capture-to-socket backlog is bounded at 1024 chunks and holding the sender defers the writer's `audio.done` until the backlog drains (pipeline.rs:133-139, :153).
service.failurePolicy: fail-soft - capture and connect failures surface as error events and the pipeline keeps running; the no-speech watchdog converts a silent session into an explicit teardown instead of a hang (xai-grok-voice/src/pipeline.rs:181-183).

service.name: workspace-rpc-client-over-a-frozen-wire-contract
service.what: The workspace surface is three crates that only work together. `WorkspaceClient` keeps a connected latch and fast-fails with `NotConnected` without a round trip, then `rpc_raw` invokes the `workspace_rpc` hub tool and drains the stream to its terminal item; a non-retryable `workspace_unavailable` maps to a distinct `WorkspaceHibernated` ("do not retry") that deliberately does not trip the latch, while `NetworkError` or a `Custom` error whose details code is `protocol_error` does (xai-grok-workspace-client/src/lib.rs:79, :87, :114-129, :203-209, :235-236, :246-257). The wire contract lives in `xai-grok-workspace-types`: every wire enum is adjacently tagged `#[serde(tag = "type", content = "data")]`, method names come from `const METHOD`, and `const ACTIVITY: RpcActivityClass` has no default so a new RPC method cannot compile without stating whether it keeps the workspace awake (xai-grok-workspace-types/src/lib.rs:23; src/rpc/mod.rs:30-60, with several dozen `workspace.*` methods each carrying a Read/Mutation classification). The response envelope carries `turn_active`, `hub_error` and `unknown_method` codes, including a matcher for the legacy `unknown workspace method:` prefix so an older hub is still understood (xai-grok-workspace-types/src/rpc/envelope.rs:13-44). `xai-grok-tools-api` is the third contract crate: generated protobuf types, shared config validation so save-time checks cannot drift from bind-time enforcement, canonical slash-command wording and the tool names that gate those commands (xai-grok-tools-api/src/lib.rs:1-9, :112-113; src/slash_commands.rs:8, :99, :105).
invariants: The connected latch is only cleared by a fatal transport error: an envelope error or a hibernation must leave it connected (xai-grok-workspace-client/src/lib.rs:235-236, :727-784).
Wire enums must stay adjacently tagged, so adding a variant cannot silently change the encoding of existing ones (xai-grok-workspace-types/src/lib.rs:23).
`ACTIVITY` has no default value, which is what forces every new RPC method to declare its idle-hibernation class (xai-grok-workspace-types/src/rpc/mod.rs:56-60).
service.failurePolicy: mixed - fail-closed on the latch (`NotConnected` with no round trip) and fail-soft otherwise: RPC errors are returned as typed envelope errors without disturbing the connection, and hibernation is a distinct non-retryable variant rather than a retryable failure (xai-grok-workspace-client/src/lib.rs:79, :203-236).

retrieval.name: hybrid-bm25-plus-vector-memory-retrieval
retrieval.what: The memory retrieval pipeline fuses lexical and vector search rather than choosing one. FTS5 BM25 runs against a supplemental evergreen query over both the global and workspace scopes so curated memory is not crowded out by session volume, optionally joined by a sqlite-vec KNN pass with an absolute L2-to-similarity normalization; per chunk the merge is `max(text_weight*fts + vector_weight*vec, fts)` so the lexical score is a floor rather than a component (xai-grok-memory/src/search.rs:183, :274-285). On top of the fused score come exponential temporal decay, per-source weights, and an access-frequency boost of `1 + ln_1p(access_count)*0.05`, then an MMR diversity re-rank before truncating to `max_results` (search.rs:323-331; xai-grok-memory/src/mmr.rs:52-62).
invariants: Ranking and MMR must use the unclamped raw score, never the clamped `SearchResult::score` - `mmr_rerank` takes a separate index-aligned relevance slice and asserts equal lengths.
Evergreen sources must keep decay at 1.0 and are the only sources subject to the scaffold-marker filter.
`&MemoryIndex` must never be held across an `.await` because rusqlite is `!Send` - which is why the pipeline is phased sync/async/sync.
Candidate generation must oversample: `candidate_limit = max_results * 3`, so the re-rank has material to work with.
retrieval.failurePolicy: mixed. Ranking degrades fail-open (FTS errors become empty via `unwrap_or_default()`, vector errors log and set `is_vector_degraded` while reporting an FTS-only mode, and a failed query embedding yields an embedding-fallback marker). Opening the index is the one hard error. Scoping a credential to an embedding endpoint fails CLOSED: an untrusted or mismatched endpoint drops the scoped credential rather than sending it.

constants.name: defaults
constants.value: max_results=6, min_score=0.7, vector_weight=0.7, text_weight=0.3; decay half_life_days=30.0; mmr enabled with lambda=0.7; dimensions=1024

retrieval.wiringNote: Wired at three call sites distinguished by a search-source enum (Tool, Injection, CompactionRecovery), but THE WHOLE SUBSYSTEM IS FLAG-GATED OFF BY DEFAULT: `enabled` is a BoolFlag whose final tier is `.default(false)` (crates/codegen/xai-grok-config-types/src/memory.rs:596-602), with `--experimental-memory`/`--no-memory` as the CLI surfaces (xai-grok-pager/src/app/cli.rs:637-650).

retrieval.name: incremental-content-hash-reindex-over-contentless-fts
retrieval.what: The markdown-to-searchable-rows write path is hash-diffed rather than rebuilt. `chunk_markdown` splits on ATX headers with paragraph and line fallbacks, short-circuits small content, overlaps continuation chunks, and prepends ancestor context as `[Context: ## A > ### B]` (xai-grok-memory/src/chunker.rs:141). `MemoryIndex::reindex_file` hashes each chunk with blake3 against existing rows keyed `"{path}:{chunk_index}"` and applies insert, update and delete plus FTS and vector maintenance inside ONE transaction (xai-grok-memory/src/index.rs:244-271, :617). Deletion is idempotent and removes a file's chunks from all three tables at once.
invariants: The chunk id must stay `"{path}:{index}"` with deterministic chunk ordering, because hash-diffing relies on positional ids.
`chunks_fts` is CONTENTLESS (`USING fts5(text, content='')`), so a delete must re-supply the original stored text - dropping the chunk text column breaks deletion.
Chunk, FTS and vector mutations must remain in one transaction, or the three tables desynchronize.
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-soft - an unreadable file warns and returns a default result, per-chunk vector deletes and upserts discard their errors, unresolvable FTS rowids are silently dropped, and a failed embedding batch is logged and skipped. Only SQL errors propagate.
retrieval.wiringNote: Wired (startup bulk reindex, per-file reindex after flush and session end, deletions after dream cleanup). sqlite-vec is registered once via `sqlite3_auto_extension`; if `SELECT vec_version()` fails the index logs once and runs FTS-only, and an embedding-dimension mismatch drops and recreates the vector table. Two sub-APIs are UNWIRED: `get_reindex_claim` and `all_indexed_paths` have zero callers, so the `memory doctor`/`reindex` flows their doc comments describe are absent (the CLI implements only `clear`), and `schema::SCHEMA_VERSION` is never read - there is no version check or rebuild path. Inherits the `GROK_MEMORY` default-false gate.

retrieval.name: bm25-fts5-session-index-with-lease-fenced-bootstrap
retrieval.what: Cross-session search over historical transcripts uses a content-synced FTS5 table: one `session_docs` row per session plus `session_docs_fts(title, content)` kept in sync by insert/delete/update triggers, so callers only ever write the base table (xai-grok-session-search/src/fts.rs:26, :565-577). Ranking is `bm25(session_docs_fts, 10.0, 1.0)` - the title weighted ten times the body. The cwd filter is applied through a JOIN rather than by indexing cwd, every token is quoted as a prefix, an AND query runs first and falls back to OR only when the AND total is zero, and UUID-like or 8-plus-hex-character queries are served through an `instr(lower(session_id), lower(?))` substring path instead of the FTS index (fts.rs:705). Full reindex is cross-process single-flight: one atomic upsert claims bootstrap when the stored stamp is expired OR in the future (clock rollback), stamping `"{unix_secs}:{uuid}"`, and every claim-scoped write is fenced on that token so a stale claimant can never assert completion or prune rows a successor indexed (bootstrap.rs:23-41).
invariants: The AND-to-OR fallback must be gated on the total estimate rather than the returned page, so every offset of one logical query uses the same MATCH string.
The completion marker may only be written while the claim token is still held.
A launch's first claim must ignore an existing marker because it owes a pruning pass, while later entrants adopt a peer's work.
cwd must stay out of the FTS table - it is a JOIN filter, not indexed content.
The title weight of 10.0 is what makes title matches outrank body matches; changing it silently reorders every result set.
retrieval.failurePolicy: mixed - fail-open at the API edge (no manager or a blank query yields an empty response), fail-closed on real query errors (they propagate), and fail-soft for bootstrap (a failed or lost bootstrap only logs, rate-limited, and the completion marker is withheld so a later search retries).

constants.name: bootstrap lease / refresh / peer wait / poll

retrieval.wiringNote: Wired into the shell and enabled by default: the `SessionSearch` feature spec has `default_enabled: true` with env `GROK_SESSION_SEARCH` (crates/codegen/xai-grok-config-types/src/registry.rs:88-94). The index lives at `<grok home>/sessions/session_search.sqlite` under a per-host effective path on network mounts. A corrupt index self-heals by QUARANTINE rather than deletion: `heal_unusable` confirms corruption with `PRAGMA integrity_check`, renames the DB and its wal/shm/journal siblings to `<name>.corrupt.<unix_nanos>` under a `<db>.lock` exclusive lock, recreates empty, bumps a cache epoch, and retries the operation exactly once (src/recovery.rs:106-170). Sessions over 30 MiB get a title-only placeholder row so title search still works and an existing fuller row is never clobbered (src/bootstrap.rs:509-535).

retrieval.name: tree-sitter-symbol-index-over-name-keyed-occurrence-map
retrieval.what: The code navigation index is built from tree-sitter queries over five grammars (rust, ts/tsx, js, go, python) whose captures are classified by naming CONVENTION - `name.definition.*` and `name.reference.*`, plus `alias.original`/`alias.name` pairs - yielding `(name, Range)` occurrences (xai-codebase-graph/src/languages/mod.rs:36, :76). `IndexBuilder` enumerates through the git index (tracked files only) with an `ignore` walker as fallback, parses on a dedicated rayon pool using thread-local parser and query caches, keeps paths repository-root-relative so the cache is portable, and persists a hand-rolled little-endian format stamped with a query hash so a query change invalidates the cache (manager/builder.rs:100-101, :238; scope_graph/graph.rs:636-638).
invariants: Capture names must keep exactly the three-part `name.definition.X` / `name.reference.X` form - the classifier matches three-element slices only.
Every file must pass the size and binary filters BEFORE a parser is constructed.
The index format version must be bumped with any layout change, because the reader hard-rejects other versions.
The reverse file-to-definitions and file-to-references maps must be updated in the same call as the forward maps, or removing a file leaks entries.
retrieval.failurePolicy: mixed - build-level fail-closed (a thread-pool creation failure is an error), per-file fail-soft (unsupported extension, empty or oversized file, a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes, an unreadable file or a parse failure all simply leave that file absent), and manager fail-open (a builder error logs and yields an EMPTY index).
retrieval.wiringNote: Wired only through a channel actor (`IndexManager`/`IndexManagerHandle`), spawned lazily on the first eligible code-navigation request, with a full-tree build running eagerly inside the actor while queries queue. THE SCOPE/EDGE GRAPH IS UNWIRED DEAD CODE: `build_scope_graph` and the only populator of the graphs map have ZERO call sites repository-wide, and the graphs map is never serialized. The shipped graph is a name-keyed occurrence map (symbol to list of relative-path and line) with bidirectional alias expansion. Host-side gating requires a web client, `x.ai/codeNavigation.enabled`, `features.codebase_indexing` (default enabled) and a git root. Note this is NOT the LSP path - the `x.ai/code/*` navigation methods route here, to tree-sitter, not to a language server.

retrieval.name: fuzzy-file-search-degradation-ladder
retrieval.what: Fuzzy path search is built as an explicit three-state degradation ladder rather than as a feature that either works or does not. `FuzzyFileMatcher` owns an `ignore` git-aware walk feeding a `nucleo` matcher, and `FuzzyFileMatcherDaemon` drives it from a background thread over a bounded channel so callers poll for the current top-k (xai-fuzzy-file-search/src/lib.rs:28-29). The states are Full (pool plus keyed matching plus browsing), BrowseOnly (the pool was refused, so keyed queries return empty but an empty-query browse still works from a serial depth-1 walk), and Disabled (the daemon worker thread was refused, so every result is empty) (lib.rs:129-158, :277-315). Thread availability is probed by actually spawning and joining N threads before building the pools (lib.rs:196).
invariants: `get()` on a Disabled daemon must report terminal-done with `generation = usize::MAX`, or a disabled search reads as perpetually pending once a query bumps the caller's minimum generation.
The thread probe must join the previous walk first so it measures freed threads.
A disabled matcher must not probe threads at all.
`Drop` must join the walk before the matcher drops.
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-soft, degrading rather than aborting - which is load-bearing because the process is built with `panic = "abort"`. An empty browse still returns results, a fully refused matcher returns empty, and a walk-thread spawn failure logs and yields no results for that walk. Errors are only ever tracing events; the public API has no error channel.

constants.name: daemon channel capacity / idle recv timeout / tick budget

retrieval.wiringNote: Wired: the single dependent is xai-grok-workspace, exposing it as a `workspace.fuzzy_search` RPC driven through a manager (xai-grok-workspace/src/file_system/mod.rs:143-166). The degradation ladder is regression-guarded by a unix child-re-exec test that caps the process-count rlimit and asserts the process degrades instead of aborting (lib.rs:843-890).

retrieval.name: confirmed-corruption-quarantine-and-recreate
retrieval.what: The session index is a rebuildable cache, so an unusable database file is classified, confirmed, quarantined and recreated instead of failing search. Classification is narrow on purpose: `is_unusable_db_error` accepts the SQLite `DatabaseCorrupt`/`NotADatabase` codes or one of three phrases - "disk image is malformed", "malformed database schema", "is not a database" - because a bare "malformed" would also match a bad FTS MATCH expression (recovery.rs:35-56). A heal is confirmed before it runs: `probe_usable` reopens the file READ-ONLY and requires `PRAGMA integrity_check` to return exactly "ok", and `heal_unusable` returns without touching anything when the reprobe says healthy or fails transiently (fts.rs:131-136; recovery.rs:138-143). Quarantine then happens under a process-wide mutex plus an exclusive cross-process `fs2` lock on `<effective db>.lock`, renaming the `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal` siblings and then the main file to `<name>.corrupt.<unix_nanos>`, recreating an empty index and bumping a process-global `CACHE_EPOCH` that long-lived connections and in-flight queries observe (recovery.rs:114-136, :64-104, :160; bootstrap.rs:419-435; manager.rs:275-285).
invariants: Corruption must be confirmed twice before anything is moved - the error-code/phrase classification AND a read-only `PRAGMA integrity_check` reprobe - because a wrong quarantine discards an index that only looked broken (fts.rs:131-136).

The phrase allowlist must stay specific: a bare "malformed" also matches a malformed FTS MATCH expression, and a test pins that neither "malformed MATCH expression" nor "database is corrupt" classifies (recovery.rs:221-233).

A heal must move the sidecars with the main file and must bump `CACHE_EPOCH`, or a stale `-wal` is replayed into the fresh database and cached connections keep pointing at the renamed inode (recovery.rs:71-84, :160; bootstrap.rs:419-424).
retrieval.failurePolicy: mixed - confirmation fails closed (nothing is quarantined unless corruption is confirmed by both the classifier and the integrity-check reprobe), while the heal itself fails soft: a heal lock that cannot be opened or taken, and a rename that fails, both leave the file in place and return, so the caller sees only the original error. The post-heal retry is bounded at exactly one attempt, and a file that is unusable but can be neither quarantined nor recreated is logged, not deleted.

constants.name: unusable-DB phrase allowlist
constants.value: "disk image is malformed" | "malformed database schema" | "is not a database"

constants.name: post-heal retry budget
constants.value: 1 (the caller's operation is re-run once against the recreated index)

retrieval.wiringNote: On every open, not behind a flag: `SessionSearchIndex::open_or_create` and `with_index` both route unusable-DB errors through `heal_unusable`, and `with_index` re-runs the caller's operation exactly once against the recreated file (fts.rs:82-102, :113-129). The heal takes its lock on the per-host effective path, so on a network mount it quarantines the same per-host file the journal-mode classifier selected (recovery.rs:118). A heal also resets the rate-limit budget of the crate's log counters, so a healed index gets a fresh warning allowance rather than staying throttled (db.rs:33-88).

retrieval.name: debounced-hash-deduped-index-maintenance
retrieval.what: Index writes are queued per session and coalesced behind a 500 ms debounce rather than written on every turn: `enqueue` sends a job to a per-grok-home worker whose pending map holds one deadline per `(session_id, cwd)` key, so repeated updates inside the window collapse into a single flush (manager.rs:32, :201-228, :304-336, :406-428). A flush re-reads the session through the `SessionSource` seam - `Some(session)` goes to `upsert_unless_unchanged`, which skips the write when the stored blake3 hash of title-plus-content matches, `None` (session gone) deletes the row, and `Err` leaves the indexed copy alone (manager.rs:430-443; doc.rs:29-61). Because that SQLite file is shared with other grok generations that may wipe or downgrade it, every query re-verifies the on-disk completed-bootstrap marker and only re-runs the full bootstrap when the marker is confirmed absent; a transient marker read failure is deliberately not a rebuild (manager.rs:1-5, :367-402; bootstrap.rs:357-367). `execute_search` waits up to 5 s for an in-flight bootstrap, then answers `bootstrapping: true` when the cache was healed, a bootstrap is running, or a live claim has no completion marker, so an empty page is not read as "no matches" (manager.rs:233-286).
invariants: The dedup hash must cover the title as well as the body (`blake3(title, NUL, content)`), or a rename with an unchanged transcript is deduped into the old title for good (doc.rs:43-51).
Only `Ok(None)` from the source may delete a row: a read error must leave the indexed copy in place, or a temporarily unreadable session store silently empties search (manager.rs:436-443).
An unreadable bootstrap marker (`None`) must not be treated as "marker absent" - rebuilding on every transient read failure means a full reindex per failing search (manager.rs:395-401).

An empty result must carry `bootstrapping: true` whenever the index may be incomplete (healed, bootstrapping, or claimed without a completion marker), so callers can tell "settling" from "no matches" (manager.rs:52-54, :280-285).
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-soft - every maintenance failure is logged, not returned: a failed upsert or extract is recorded against the session and the worker moves on, a failed bootstrap only logs through a rate-limited counter and withholds the completion marker so a later search retries, and queries degrade to an empty (not final) response when no manager exists or the query is blank.
retrieval.wiringNote: Wired: the shell enqueues after a turn's persistence write (xai-grok-shell/src/session/persistence.rs:2005-2010) and when a session title is generated or reset (src/extensions/session_admin.rs:181-186, :301-305). A process that keeps no index holds no manager, and the shell models that as a three-state decision - `IndexDecision::Pending` answers `still_settling()` rather than an empty final page, `Off` is final, `On` carries the manager (xai-grok-shell/src/session/storage/search.rs:66-102, :192-203). `evict_session` returns without doing anything when no index file exists, so a process that only evicts never creates one (manager.rs:288-302).

retrieval.name: two-tier-index-lock-with-stale-takeover
retrieval.what: Index work on a repository is serialized twice over: an in-memory `DashMap` registry dedups inside the process with shared, counted readers for `Load` and a single exclusive writer for `Save`/`Build`/`BackgroundRefresh`, and an exclusive operation then writes a cross-process lock file beside the cache carrying `operation=`, `pid=`, `started=` and `workspace=` (lock.rs:23-26, :53-58, :86, :170-221, :325-380). An existing lock file is honored only while it is younger than the operation's own stale timeout AND its recorded PID is still alive; otherwise it is logged as stale and taken over, and a failed cross-process acquisition releases the in-memory lock before reporting `Busy` (lock.rs:331-350, :406-419, :198-212). `is_operation_in_progress` exposes the same rule as a non-blocking probe that acquires nothing (lock.rs:226-254). The shipped consumer is the background index refresh, which returns early - no stat pass, no filesystem walk - whenever the lock is busy (index_manager.rs:1321-1336).
invariants: The shared/exclusive asymmetry is the mechanism: `Load` counts readers while every other operation is exclusive, so a `Load` that blocks other loads, or an exclusive that coexists with a reader, silently re-admits duplicate index work (lock.rs:53-58, :270-300).
Staleness requires BOTH signals - an expired per-operation timeout and a dead PID on unix; on non-unix `is_process_alive` reports true, so only the timeout can break a lock there (lock.rs:406-419).
A failed cross-process acquisition must release the in-memory lock, or the workspace stays locked to this process for the rest of its life (lock.rs:198-212).
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-soft - contention is never an error: `try_lock` returns `LockResult::Busy { operation, holder_pid }` and the caller skips the work (the background refresh logs and returns). A lock directory that cannot be created only warns, a lock file that cannot be written reports busy, removal on drop only warns, and the non-unix PID probe conservatively reports every process alive rather than guessing.

constants.name: per-operation stale timeouts
constants.value: load 120 s / save 120 s / build 600 s / background_refresh 300 s

retrieval.wiringNote: One operation is wired today: `try_lock(root_path, IndexOperation::BackgroundRefresh)` in the background index refresh (index_manager.rs:1322), which is what stops two grok processes from stat-walking and re-parsing the same repository at once. The `Load`, `Save` and `Build` variants and the exported `is_operation_in_progress` probe have no call sites outside lock.rs's own tests in this tree (repo-wide grep), so the indexing actor's own cache load/save path does not take these locks.

ops.name: three-mode-telemetry-policy-gate
ops.what: One mode decides whether anything is emitted at all. `TelemetryMode` is `Disabled | SessionMetrics | Enabled`, and `Disabled` is the `#[default]`, so telemetry is off unless it is explicitly turned on (xai-grok-telemetry/src/config.rs:5, :11-13). Parsing accepts the legacy bool plus the string `session-metrics` / `session_metrics` for the middle mode, and `Display` writes the mode back so a parent can hand `GROK_TELEMETRY_ENABLED={mode}` to spawned children (config.rs:32, :40, :61). Emission sites consult the narrowest predicate: `log_event` needs `client::is_enabled()` (full `Enabled`), `log_session_event` needs `is_session_metrics_enabled()` (either non-disabled mode), and Mixpanel profile sync needs `is_enabled()` only (client.rs:138, :146-151; session_ctx.rs:168-171). `log_event_dual(internal_enabled, data)` exists so a caller with a stricter internal gate still fans out to the external stream exactly once (session_ctx.rs:157). `TelemetryConfig::apply_env_overrides` layers `GROK_TELEMETRY_EVENTS_URL`, `_EVENTS_API_KEY`, `_MIXPANEL_TOKEN`, `_MIXPANEL_ENABLED` and `_TRACE_UPLOAD` over file and remote config, and Mixpanel defaults on only when a build token was baked in (config.rs:192, :236-248). The enterprise posture is the default: `Disabled` unless an operator turns it on, and an unrecognized mode string degrades to `Disabled` with a warning rather than enabling anything (config.rs:12-13, :46).
invariants: `TelemetryMode::Disabled` must stay the `#[default]` - telemetry is opt-in (xai-grok-telemetry/src/config.rs:12-13).
`is_enabled()` and `is_session_metrics_enabled()` must read the installed client, never the requested mode (client.rs:138, :146-151).
`log_event_dual` must fan out to the external stream before the internal gate, because that stream is independent of `TelemetryMode` (session_ctx.rs:157).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-open in the safe direction - an unrecognized mode string warns and lands on `Disabled`, every emission path early-returns, and nothing errors (xai-grok-telemetry/src/config.rs:46).
ops.wiringNote: Two functions in `id.rs` are inert: `has_workspace_env_markers` (id.rs:156) and the `GROK_TELEMETRY_SPECIAL_USER` gate `is_special_user` (id.rs:161-163) exist but the special-user gate has no shipped caller, so it is dead code today.

ops.name: typed-event-emission-with-fire-and-forget-exit-drain
ops.what: Events are typed structs registered through the `telemetry_event!` macro rather than free-form strings, and delivery is fire-and-forget with a bounded exit drain. `log_event` and `log_session_event` funnel into `emit_event_with_origin`, which snapshots the ambient session context, prefixes the event name with the emitter's origin, and spawns the post; in-flight posts are counted by a `PENDING_EVENTS` atomic through an RAII guard (xai-grok-telemetry/src/session_ctx.rs:202, :317; xai-grok-telemetry/src/events/mod.rs:2). `drain_pending(timeout)` polls that counter until it reaches zero or the deadline passes, and the drain is entrypoint-gated: one-shot entrypoints drain at session exit within `SESSION_EXIT_DRAIN`, while interactive hosts deliberately do not (session_ctx.rs:221-246). Event names are reserved against `RESERVED_EVENT_KEYS` so an event payload cannot overwrite an injected key (client.rs:2-3, :252). Local diagnostics are separate and env-gated: `unified.jsonl` under the grok home is capped at 5 MiB, the writer rechecks its own inode every 2 s, and trimming rewrites the tail in place under an exclusive advisory lock so concurrent appenders keep a live file (xai-grok-telemetry/src/unified_log.rs:27-28, :120, :334-338).
invariants: The pending counter must be decremented on every exit path, including a cancelled or never-polled post, or the drain would wait out its whole budget (xai-grok-telemetry/src/session_ctx.rs:202, :246).
Registration must happen after the runtime check, so a dropped event cannot pin the counter above zero for the life of the process (session_ctx.rs:317).
`unified.jsonl` trimming must stay in place under the exclusive lock, never a delete-and-recreate, or open appenders would keep writing to an unlinked inode (unified_log.rs:334-338).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-soft - telemetry loss always beats blocking: with no Tokio runtime the event is dropped rather than panicking, the drain gives up at its deadline, and there is no retry or persistence (xai-grok-telemetry/src/session_ctx.rs:221-246).

constants.name: unified log file / size cap / maintenance interval

ops.wiringNote: There is no bounded queue, no batching and no drop-on-full in this crate - product events are unbounded `tokio::spawn` posts. The bounded-queue and circuit-breaker behaviour for trace uploads lives in `xai-file-utils` (queue.rs), which the shell's upload path calls, not here.

ops.name: dual-analytics-sink-with-minimal-mixpanel-client
ops.what: `client::track` is the single analytics emitter and it fans out to two independent sinks. It first attaches identity and a 20-field `EventEnrichment` snapshot (os, arch, cpu share and time, memory, uptime, CI flag, entrypoint, interactivity, release channel, dev build) to the event (xai-grok-telemetry/src/client.rs:183). The product-events sink fires only when both a URL and an API key are configured, and the Mixpanel sink only when a Mixpanel client was built, which requires `mixpanel_enabled` plus a token (client.rs:82, :322, :356). `event_value` strips the emitter prefix so shell and workspace events collapse to one bare suffix (client.rs:23). `xai-mixpanel` is deliberately minimal: base64 of the JSON array form-POSTed to `api.mixpanel.com/track` (and `engage`) with a 10 s timeout and an injectable `reqwest::Client`, because `mixpanel-rs` would pull a second reqwest version into the binary (xai-mixpanel/src/lib.rs:1-6, :27, :63-86). Property strings are scrubbed for secrets *before* the project token is injected, so the token itself - which is deliberately Bearer-shaped - is not redacted (xai-mixpanel/src/lib.rs:47-59).
invariants: Each sink fires only when its own configuration is complete: product events need url plus key, Mixpanel needs the enabled flag plus a token (xai-grok-telemetry/src/client.rs:322, :356).
The Mixpanel token must be injected after the scrub, or the token is redacted out of every payload (xai-mixpanel/src/lib.rs:47-59).
`event_value` must strip exactly one leading emitter prefix; the prefixes are asserted mutually exclusive (xai-grok-telemetry/src/client.rs:23, :687).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-soft - both posts are fire-and-forget; an analytics failure is logged and cannot affect the turn (xai-mixpanel/src/lib.rs:63-86).

ops.name: external-otel-stream-behind-a-fail-closed-privacy-gate
ops.what: An opt-in OTLP stream to the customer's own collector, activated only by a double opt-in: `GROK_EXTERNAL_OTEL` must be set *and* a real exporter must be selected in `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` or `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, otherwise resolution returns nothing and no exporter, thread or socket is created (xai-grok-telemetry/src/external/config.rs:5, :41, :392; xai-grok-telemetry/src/external/mod.rs:4, :16). Construction also refuses to activate when the internal pipeline already consumed the shared `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables, which prevents double-exporting the same events (external/mod.rs:160). The privacy boundary is enforced twice: at emit time by a scrub, and at export time by validators that inspect each record and metric and DROP a violating record or the whole metric export rather than scrubbing in place, because the SDK types are not mutable from an exporter wrapper (external/redact.rs:4, :56; external/emit.rs:99). Content is additionally capped: strings collapse to a 512-character prefix and JSON depth, collection size and byte budgets are bounded (external/truncate.rs:6). Emission also sits behind a fail-closed settings gate that opens when settings resolve or after a bounded wait, and remote policy may only tighten - force-disable or lock content gates, never enable (external/mod.rs:263, :388).
invariants: Default off: with the master switch unset or no exporter selected, nothing is constructed - zero allocation, zero threads, zero sockets (xai-grok-telemetry/src/external/mod.rs:16).
Remote policy has no enable direction; it may only force-disable or tighten content gates (external/mod.rs:388).
A record that fails the content gate must be dropped, never scrubbed at export time, because the SDK read path is immutable (external/redact.rs:4, :56).
ops.failurePolicy: mixed - fail-closed on privacy and schema violations (silent drop with health counters), fail-open on activation (the stream is simply absent), and bounded-open on the settings gate (a 30 s ceiling, then it proceeds under local config).
ops.wiringNote: Related but distinct: the internal OTLP trace pipeline and the Sentry path share the same redaction primitives (`redact_common`), and Sentry is configured with `send_default_pii: false`, a 0.01 trace sample rate and a `before_send` scrubber (xai-grok-telemetry/src/sentry.rs:10, :39-53, :193).

ops.name: crash-handler-with-postmortem-capture-and-archive
ops.what: `install()` registers one `sigaction` for SIGBUS, SIGSEGV and SIGABRT with `SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK | SA_RESETHAND`, saves the terminal state, and allocates a 16 KiB alternate signal stack via mmap so a stack-overflow fault still has somewhere to run (xai-crash-handler/src/handler.rs:195-212, :228-250, :297-310). The handler writes a fixed-layout binary blob - magic `GCRX`, version 1, at most 64 frames, header 59 bytes, whole file at most 571 bytes - into a pre-allocated `.bss` buffer, so it never allocates (xai-crash-handler/src/format.rs:1-33; handler.rs:195-196). SIGABRT is hooked on purpose because `panic = "abort"` builds - every shipped release - terminate through `abort(3)`, so a Rust panic otherwise leaves nothing; Windows captures access violations through the unhandled-exception filter and has no SIGABRT arm (handler.rs:3-8; xai-crash-handler/src/lib.rs:1-8). The handler then restores the terminal through raw async-signal-safe writes and re-raises with the default disposition, preserving exit status and core dumps (xai-crash-handler/src/terminal.rs:41-61; handler.rs:252-281). At the next startup `check_previous_crash` parses the blob, symbolicates the frames, writes `last-crash-report.txt` owner-only, archives to `history/crash-<timestamp>.txt` keeping the last five, and deletes the blob so it is processed once (lib.rs:43, :122-149, :181-203).
invariants: `check_previous_crash` must run before `install`, because install opens the blob with truncation and would erase the previous crash (xai-crash-handler/src/lib.rs:12-15).
Only async-signal-safe work belongs in the handler: raw `write(2)` on a static buffer, no allocation (xai-crash-handler/src/format.rs:1-4; terminal.rs:48-61).
Crash reports must stay owner-only 0600, including a pre-existing looser file, because they carry source paths and backtraces (lib.rs:151-179).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-soft - `install` returns false on any failure (unsupported platform, mkdir/open error) rather than aborting startup, and report-writing errors are ignored so a crash report can never mask the crash itself (xai-crash-handler/src/lib.rs:79-83, :132-138).

ops.name: smoke-test-verified-self-update-with-atomic-activation
ops.what: Self-update converges the on-disk install to the channel pointer, and its integrity gate is execution rather than a hash. There is no checksum or signature verification: the crate's own comment states that downloads are verified by a smoke test, not a checksum, which is exactly why `GROK_CLI_BASE_URL` is honoured only for a parsed loopback URL - a userinfo trick such as `http://127.0.0.1:9@evil.com` is rejected by parsing the URL rather than prefix-matching it (xai-grok-update/src/version.rs:27-57). Channel pointers resolve to a plain-text semver at a primary Cloudflare-fronted base with a direct-GCS fallback, and for the alpha channel both pointers are fetched and the semver-greater wins (version.rs:16-25, :251-291). A download streams into a unique temp sibling (`<name>.{pid}-{seq}.tmp`, so two racing updaters can never rename each other's half-written file), gets `+x` *before* the rename onto the destination so a concurrent installer never execs a 0644 file, and is renamed atomically into place (auto_update.rs:998-1034). The smoke test is bounded at 30 s with eight ETXTBSY retries at a 25 ms base backoff, downloads carry a 20-minute request budget and are swept only after an hour of staleness, parallel byte-range fetching needs at least 16 MiB and clamps to 8 chunks, and decoded archives are capped so a crafted bundle cannot fill the disk (auto_update.rs:983-1042, :1309, :1453-1460). Windows cannot write a running executable, so activation renames the destination aside and rolls the rename back if the copy fails (auto_update.rs:1990-2065).
invariants: Activation must stay atomic and per-racer: the temp name is unique per process and the `+x` mode is set before the rename, or a concurrent updater could exec a partially published binary (xai-grok-update/src/auto_update.rs:998-1034).
A non-loopback `GROK_CLI_BASE_URL` must stay ignored; with no checksum in the pipeline, an arbitrary base would serve a hijacked install (xai-grok-update/src/version.rs:27-40).
Stale-artifact sweeping must wait at least `STALE_TMP_AGE`, because deleting a concurrent updater's in-flight download makes its atomic rename fail (auto_update.rs:983-988).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-closed on install - a candidate that fails the smoke test is never activated and the running version is unchanged - with a soft landing on the platform's inability to replace a running binary, where the destination is renamed aside and the rename is rolled back if the copy fails (xai-grok-update/src/auto_update.rs:2038-2065).

ops.name: compile-time-version-stamping-with-runtime-commit-injection
ops.what: The installed version is a compile-time constant: `VERSION` is `option_env!("GROK_VERSION")` when the release pipeline injects it and falls back to `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` otherwise, and `IS_DEV_BUILD` is exactly the absence of that injection, so a from-source build is self-identifying (xai-grok-version/src/lib.rs:9-15). The short commit is injected at runtime instead of compiled into every library, because only the release binary stamps and calls `set_full_version` at startup; the value lives in a `OnceLock` where the first set wins and repeats are ignored, so the lib crates do not recompile on every commit (lib.rs:17-30). `installed()` honours a trimmed `GROK_TEST_VERSION` override and `installed_semver()` parses the result, which is what lets version policy be tested without a release (lib.rs:7, :32-42). Display helpers append a pre-formatted channel label (" [alpha]", " [stable]" or empty) supplied by the update crate (lib.rs:44-53).
invariants: `VERSION` and `IS_DEV_BUILD` must stay `const` and derived from the same `option_env!` call, so a build without injection is consistently a dev build (xai-grok-version/src/lib.rs:9-15).
`set_full_version` must stay first-set-wins and idempotent; a later call must not rewrite the stamp (lib.rs:21-25, pinned by test at :87-94).
The channel label stays a caller-supplied suffix; this crate must not do network I/O to compute it (lib.rs:44-53).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-open - the version string is never absent: without injection it degrades to `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, and `full_version()` falls back to plain `VERSION` when no binary has stamped a commit (xai-grok-version/src/lib.rs:14-15, :27-30).

ops.name: timestamped-and-timed-tracing-macros
ops.what: Two small macro families give headless-safe diagnostics without a terminal. `tprintln!` emits `{unix_seconds}::{message}` at info level and `teprintln!` does the same at warn, both through `tracing` so they are safe with no TTY attached, with `format_args!` forwarded straight through and a pre-epoch clock yielding `0` instead of a panic (xai-tracing-macros/src/timestamp.rs:1-4, :20-35, :51-66). `timed!` measures a block with `Instant` and either returns `(value, elapsed_ms)` or logs the elapsed time at a caller-chosen level (debug by default); its `try:` arms log the error as a field on the error path and return the original `Result` unchanged, in sync and async forms (xai-tracing-macros/src/timed.rs:1-13, :23-28, :49-63, :84-98). The macros are `#[macro_export]`ed from the crate root through two private modules (src/lib.rs:28-29).
invariants: The timestamp is Unix **seconds** and the separator is exactly `::`; the no-argument arm still emits the trailing separator (xai-tracing-macros/src/timestamp.rs:21-34).
`timed!` must return the wrapped block's value - or the original `Result`, error included - so it stays drop-in inside existing code (timed.rs:23-28, :53-62).
`elapsed_ms` is recorded as `u64` and error arms add an `error` field, which is the machine-readable part of the contract (timed.rs:16-21).
ops.failurePolicy: fail-open - a failing system clock yields timestamp 0 rather than panicking, and timing never alters the wrapped block's result (xai-tracing-macros/src/timestamp.rs:22-26).

constants.name: logged fields
constants.value: elapsed_ms (u64), error (?err on the error arm)
